answer: The prover commits to a set inclusion proof over the registry of claimants, and the proof is small because it carries the exclusion of every competing holder, so two identities claiming the same resource would have to produce contradictory proofs. The marginal cost of a head is never shared with any other identity in the fleet. The haven is the unique resource, the whisper the proof that excludes every other holder, and the timber the registry that makes the exclusion checkable; cloning the haven forces two contradictory whisper proofs, and the timber is where the contradiction shows.
